NKJV.1: Now the whole earth had one language and one speech.
NKJV.2: And it came to pass, as they journeyed from the east, that they found a plain in the land of Shinar, and they dwelt there.
NKJV.3: Then they said to one another, “Come, let us make bricks and bake them thoroughly.” They had brick for stone, and they had asphalt for mortar.
NKJV.4: And they said, “Come, let us build ourselves a city, and a tower whose top is in the heavens; let us make a name for ourselves, lest we be scattered abroad over the face of the whole earth.”
NKJV.5: But the LORD came down to see the city and the tower which the sons of men had built.
NKJV.6: And the LORD said, “Indeed the people are one and they all have one language, and this is what they begin to do; now nothing that they propose to do will be withheld from them.
NKJV.7: Come, let Us go down and there confuse their language, that they may not understand one another’s speech.”
NKJV.8: So the LORD scattered them abroad from there over the face of all the earth, and they ceased building the city.
NKJV.9: Therefore its name is called Babel, because there the LORD confused the language of all the earth; and from there the LORD scattered them abroad over the face of all the earth.
NKJV.10: This is the genealogy of Shem: Shem was one hundred years old, and begot Arphaxad two years after the flood.
NKJV.11: After he begot Arphaxad, Shem lived five hundred years, and begot sons and daughters.
NKJV.12: Arphaxad lived thirty-five years, and begot Salah.
NKJV.13: After he begot Salah, Arphaxad lived four hundred and three years, and begot sons and daughters.
NKJV.14: Salah lived thirty years, and begot Eber.
NKJV.15: After he begot Eber, Salah lived four hundred and three years, and begot sons and daughters.
NKJV.16: Eber lived thirty-four years, and begot Peleg.
NKJV.17: After he begot Peleg, Eber lived four hundred and thirty years, and begot sons and daughters.
NKJV.18: Peleg lived thirty years, and begot Reu.
NKJV.19: After he begot Reu, Peleg lived two hundred and nine years, and begot sons and daughters.
NKJV.20: Reu lived thirty-two years, and begot Serug.
NKJV.21: After he begot Serug, Reu lived two hundred and seven years, and begot sons and daughters.
NKJV.22: Serug lived thirty years, and begot Nahor.
NKJV.23: After he begot Nahor, Serug lived two hundred years, and begot sons and daughters.
NKJV.24: Nahor lived twenty-nine years, and begot Terah.
NKJV.25: After he begot Terah, Nahor lived one hundred and nineteen years, and begot sons and daughters.
NKJV.26: Now Terah lived seventy years, and begot Abram, Nahor, and Haran.
NKJV.27: This is the genealogy of Terah: Terah begot Abram, Nahor, and Haran. Haran begot Lot.
NKJV.28: And Haran died before his father Terah in his native land, in Ur of the Chaldeans.
NKJV.29: Then Abram and Nahor took wives: the name of Abram’s wife was Sarai, and the name of Nahor’s wife, Milcah, the daughter of Haran the father of Milcah and the father of Iscah.
NKJV.30: But  Sarai was barren; she had no child.
NKJV.31: And Terah took his son Abram and his grandson Lot, the son of Haran, and his daughter-in-law Sarai, his son Abram’s wife, and they went out with them from Ur of the Chaldeans to go to the land of Canaan; and they came to Haran and dwelt there.
NKJV.32: So the days of Terah were two hundred and five years, and Terah died in Haran.

ESV.1: Now the whole earth had one language and the same words.
ESV.2: And as people migrated from the east, they found a plain in the land of Shinar and settled there.
ESV.3: And they said to one another, “Come, let us make bricks, and burn them thoroughly.” And they had brick for stone, and bitumen for mortar.
ESV.4: Then they said, “Come, let us build ourselves a city and a tower with its top in the heavens, and let us make a name for ourselves, lest we be dispersed over the face of the whole earth.”
ESV.5: And the LORD came down to see the city and the tower, which the children of man had built.
ESV.6: And the LORD said, “Behold, they are one people, and they have all one language, and this is only the beginning of what they will do. And nothing that they propose to do will now be impossible for them.
ESV.7: Come, let us go down and there confuse their language, so that they may not understand one another's speech.”
ESV.8: So the LORD dispersed them from there over the face of all the earth, and they left off building the city.
ESV.9: Therefore its name was called Babel, because there the LORD confused  the language of all the earth. And from there the LORD dispersed them over the face of all the earth.
ESV.10: These are the generations of Shem. When Shem was 100 years old, he fathered Arpachshad two years after the flood.
ESV.11: And Shem lived after he fathered Arpachshad 500 years and had other sons and daughters.
ESV.12: When Arpachshad had lived 35 years, he fathered Shelah.
ESV.13: And Arpachshad lived after he fathered Shelah 403 years and had other sons and daughters.
ESV.14: When Shelah had lived 30 years, he fathered Eber.
ESV.15: And Shelah lived after he fathered Eber 403 years and had other sons and daughters.
ESV.16: When Eber had lived 34 years, he fathered Peleg.
ESV.17: And Eber lived after he fathered Peleg 430 years and had other sons and daughters.
ESV.18: When Peleg had lived 30 years, he fathered Reu.
ESV.19: And Peleg lived after he fathered Reu 209 years and had other sons and daughters.
ESV.20: When Reu had lived 32 years, he fathered Serug.
ESV.21: And Reu lived after he fathered Serug 207 years and had other sons and daughters.
ESV.22: When Serug had lived 30 years, he fathered Nahor.
ESV.23: And Serug lived after he fathered Nahor 200 years and had other sons and daughters.
ESV.24: When Nahor had lived 29 years, he fathered Terah.
ESV.25: And Nahor lived after he fathered Terah 119 years and had other sons and daughters.
ESV.26: When Terah had lived 70 years, he fathered Abram, Nahor, and Haran.
ESV.27: Now these are the generations of Terah. Terah fathered Abram, Nahor, and Haran; and Haran fathered Lot.
ESV.28: Haran died in the presence of his father Terah in the land of his kindred, in Ur of the Chaldeans.
ESV.29: And Abram and Nahor took wives. The name of Abram's wife was Sarai, and the name of Nahor's wife, Milcah, the daughter of Haran the father of Milcah and Iscah.
ESV.30: Now Sarai was barren; she had no child.
ESV.31: Terah took Abram his son and Lot the son of Haran, his grandson, and Sarai his daughter-in-law, his son Abram's wife, and they went forth together from Ur of the Chaldeans to go into the land of Canaan, but when they came to Haran, they settled there.
ESV.32: The days of Terah were 205 years, and Terah died in Haran.

NLT.1: At one time all the people of the world spoke the same language and used the same words.
NLT.2: As the people migrated to the east, they found a plain in the land of Babylonia and settled there.
NLT.3: They began saying to each other, “Let’s make bricks and harden them with fire.” (In this region bricks were used instead of stone, and tar was used for mortar.)
NLT.4: Then they said, “Come, let’s build a great city for ourselves with a tower that reaches into the sky. This will make us famous and keep us from being scattered all over the world.”
NLT.5: But the LORD came down to look at the city and the tower the people were building.
NLT.6: “Look!” he said. “The people are united, and they all speak the same language. After this, nothing they set out to do will be impossible for them!
NLT.7: Come, let’s go down and confuse the people with different languages. Then they won’t be able to understand each other.”
NLT.8: In that way, the LORD scattered them all over the world, and they stopped building the city.
NLT.9: That is why the city was called Babel, because that is where the LORD confused the people with different languages. In this way he scattered them all over the world.
NLT.10: This is the account of Shem’s family. Two years after the great flood, when Shem was 100 years old, he became the father of Arphaxad.
NLT.11: After the birth of Arphaxad, Shem lived another 500 years and had other sons and daughters.
NLT.12: When Arphaxad was 35 years old, he became the father of Shelah.
NLT.13: After the birth of Shelah, Arphaxad lived another 403 years and had other sons and daughters.
NLT.14: When Shelah was 30 years old, he became the father of Eber.
NLT.15: After the birth of Eber, Shelah lived another 403 years and had other sons and daughters.
NLT.16: When Eber was 34 years old, he became the father of Peleg.
NLT.17: After the birth of Peleg, Eber lived another 430 years and had other sons and daughters.
NLT.18: When Peleg was 30 years old, he became the father of Reu.
NLT.19: After the birth of Reu, Peleg lived another 209 years and had other sons and daughters.
NLT.20: When Reu was 32 years old, he became the father of Serug.
NLT.21: After the birth of Serug, Reu lived another 207 years and had other sons and daughters.
NLT.22: When Serug was 30 years old, he became the father of Nahor.
NLT.23: After the birth of Nahor, Serug lived another 200 years and had other sons and daughters.
NLT.24: When Nahor was 29 years old, he became the father of Terah.
NLT.25: After the birth of Terah, Nahor lived another 119 years and had other sons and daughters.
NLT.26: After Terah was 70 years old, he became the father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran.
NLT.27: This is the account of Terah’s family. Terah was the father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran; and Haran was the father of Lot.
NLT.28: But Haran died in Ur of the Chaldeans, the land of his birth, while his father, Terah, was still living.
NLT.29: Meanwhile, Abram and Nahor both married. The name of Abram’s wife was Sarai, and the name of Nahor’s wife was Milcah. (Milcah and her sister Iscah were daughters of Nahor’s brother Haran.)
NLT.30: But Sarai was unable to become pregnant and had no children.
NLT.31: One day Terah took his son Abram, his daughter-in-law Sarai (his son Abram’s wife), and his grandson Lot (his son Haran’s child) and moved away from Ur of the Chaldeans. He was headed for the land of Canaan, but they stopped at Haran and settled there.
NLT.32: Terah lived for 205 years and died while still in Haran.

WEB.1: The whole earth was of one language and of one speech.
WEB.2: As they traveled east, they found a plain in the land of Shinar, and they lived there.
WEB.3: They said to one another, “Come, let’s make bricks, and burn them thoroughly.” They had brick for stone, and they used tar for mortar.
WEB.4: They said, “Come, let’s build ourselves a city, and a tower whose top reaches to the sky, and let’s make a name for ourselves, lest we be scattered abroad on the surface of the whole earth.”
WEB.5: Yahweh came down to see the city and the tower, which the children of men built.
WEB.6: Yahweh said, “Behold, they are one people, and they have all one language, and this is what they begin to do. Now nothing will be withheld from them, which they intend to do.
WEB.7: Come, let’s go down, and there confuse their language, that they may not understand one another’s speech.”

AMP.1: Now the whole earth spoke one language and used the same words (vocabulary).
AMP.2: And as people journeyed eastward, they found a plain in the land of Shinar and they settled there.
AMP.3: They said one to another, "Come, let us make bricks and fire them thoroughly [in a kiln, to harden and strengthen them]." So they used brick for stone [as building material], and they used tar (bitumen, asphalt) for mortar.
AMP.4: They said, "Come, let us build a city for ourselves, and a tower whose top will reach into the heavens, and let us make a [famous] name for ourselves, so that we will not be scattered [into separate groups] and be dispersed over the surface of the entire earth [as the LORD instructed]."
AMP.5: Now the LORD came down to see the city and the tower which the sons of men had built.
AMP.6: And the LORD said, "Behold, they are one [unified] people, and they all have the same language. This is only the beginning of what they will do [in rebellion against Me], and now no evil thing they imagine they can do will be impossible for them.
AMP.7: Come, let Us (Father, Son, Holy Spirit) go down and there confuse and mix up their language, so that they will not understand one another's speech."
AMP.8: So the LORD scattered them abroad from there over the surface of the entire earth; and they stopped building the city.
AMP.9: Therefore the name of the city was Babel—because there the LORD confused the language of the entire earth; and from that place the LORD scattered and dispersed them over the surface of all the earth.
AMP.10: These are the records of the generations of Shem [from whom Abraham descended]. Shem was a hundred years old when he became the father of Arpachshad, two years after the flood.
AMP.11: And Shem lived five hundred years after Arpachshad was born, and he had other sons and daughters.
AMP.12: When Arpachshad had lived thirty-five years, he became the father of Shelah.
AMP.13: Arpachshad lived four hundred and three years after Shelah was born, and he had other sons and daughters.
AMP.14: When Shelah had lived thirty years, he became the father of Eber.
AMP.15: Shelah lived four hundred and three years after Eber was born, and he had other sons and daughters.
AMP.16: When Eber had lived thirty-four years, he became the father of Peleg.
AMP.17: And Eber lived four hundred and thirty years after Peleg was born, and he had other sons and daughters.
AMP.18: When Peleg had lived thirty years, he became the father of Reu.
AMP.19: And Peleg lived two hundred and nine years after Reu was born, and he had other sons and daughters.
AMP.20: When Reu had lived thirty-two years, he became the father of Serug.
AMP.21: And Reu lived two hundred and seven years after Serug was born, and he had other sons and daughters.
AMP.22: When Serug had lived thirty years, he became the father of Nahor.
AMP.23: And Serug lived two hundred years after Nahor was born, and he had other sons and daughters.
AMP.24: When Nahor had lived twenty-nine years, he became the father of Terah.
AMP.25: And Nahor lived a hundred and nineteen years after Terah was born, and he had other sons and daughters.
AMP.26: After Terah had lived seventy years, he became the father of Abram and Nahor and Haran [his firstborn].
AMP.27: Now these are the records of the descendants of Terah. Terah was the father of Abram (Abraham), Nahor, and Haran; and Haran was the father of Lot.
AMP.28: Haran died before his father Terah in the land of his birth, in Ur of the Chaldeans.
AMP.29: Abram and Nahor took wives for themselves. The name of Abram's wife was Sarai (later called Sarah), and the name of Nahor's wife was Milcah, the daughter of Haran, the father of Milcah and Iscah.
AMP.30: But Sarai was barren; she did not have a child.
AMP.31: Terah took Abram his son, and Lot the son of Haran, his grandson, and Sarai his daughter-in-law, his son Abram's wife; and they went out together to go from Ur of the Chaldeans into the land of Canaan; but when they came to Haran [about five hundred and fifty miles northwest of Ur], they settled there.
AMP.32: Terah lived two hundred and five years; and Terah died in Haran.
